def: Training many models on bootstrap samples of the data and averaging their predictions to reduce variance.
A sample of n rows drawn with replacement from n rows, which leaves out about 37 percent of the distinct rows.
The error of each row predicted using only the trees whose bootstrap sample did not include it, a free validation estimate for bagged models.
A bagged ensemble of deep trees that also considers only a random subset of features at each split, to decorrelate the trees.
Building a model as a sum of weak learners added one at a time, each trained to correct the errors of the sum so far.
Boosting in which each new tree is fitted to the negative gradient of the loss with respect to the current predictions.
The negative gradient of the loss at a row's current prediction, which equals the ordinary residual for squared error.
The factor by which each new tree is scaled before being added to a boosted model, trading more rounds for better generalisation.
Halting boosting when validation error has not improved for a set number of rounds, so the number of trees is chosen from data.
The second derivative of the loss with respect to a prediction, used with the gradient to take a Newton-style step in XGBoost.
A regularised, second-order gradient-boosting library with sparsity-aware splits and a fast, scalable implementation.
A gradient-boosting library built for speed on large data, using histogram splits, leaf-wise growth, GOSS and feature bundling.
A gradient-boosting library that encodes categorical features with ordered target statistics and builds symmetric trees.
A target encoding computed for each row only from rows earlier in a random order, so a row never sees its own label.
